transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I suppose what brings me in is mostly my wife, if I’m being honest. She’s been fussing that I’m not eating enough, and she thought I ought to come in and talk to someone. I don’t really see it as such a big thing, but she gets worried.

Most mornings I’ll have coffee and maybe a piece of toast, and that feels like plenty to get me going. Then later in the day I might have a bit of soup, or some vegetables, something light like that. I don’t really feel the need for a big meal anymore. At my age, sitting down to a large plate of food just feels unnecessary, almost more than I want to deal with. But she sees it and thinks I’m skipping meals or not taking care of myself, so… here I am.
Would you say that you're eating less because food doesn’t appeal to you, or more because you're intentionally choosing to eat less?

I’d say it’s more that I’m choosing to eat less, though I don’t really think of it in such a deliberate way. Food isn’t exactly unpleasant to me, it’s just… big meals feel unnecessary now. At my age I don’t feel like I need all that.

Most days I’ll have my coffee in the morning, maybe a piece of toast, and that honestly feels like enough to start the day. Then later I might have some soup or a few vegetables, something light. I don’t sit there thinking, “I must not eat,” it’s more that a full plate seems like too much bother, too much food, more than I want. My wife sees it and thinks I’m not eating enough, but to me it just feels sensible.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I have quiet days, same as anyone my age, and I suppose I’m not as busy as I used to be, but I wouldn’t say I feel sad all the time or anything like that.

As for losing interest… I don’t know. I still like the things I like, in my own way. I still read the paper, watch a bit of television, potter around the house. Maybe I do less than I did years ago, but that feels more like getting older than some kind of gloom, if that makes sense.

My wife might say I’m more withdrawn, but I don’t feel especially down. I just like things quieter now.
Have you noticed feeling more tired than usual or having a lack of energy, even if you’re not doing much?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way, no. I mean, I’m 78, so of course I’m not bouncing around like I did when I was younger. If I sit in the chair after lunch, I might doze a little, but I always thought that was fairly normal. My wife sometimes says I seem slower, but she says that about all sorts of things these days.

I don’t feel completely exhausted or anything dramatic. I still get up, get dressed, do bits around the house, make my coffee, read the paper, that sort of thing. I suppose I take things at a slower pace, but I haven’t really noticed some big lack of energy. It’s more just… I don’t rush anymore.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus, make decisions, or think clearly lately?

I can’t say I’ve noticed anything in particular, no. I mean, I suppose I’m not as quick with things as I used to be, but that’s been gradual, just part of being older, I’d have thought.

I still read the paper and follow what’s going on, though sometimes I’ll read an article and then go back over a bit of it if it’s long or full of politics and numbers. But I wouldn’t say I’m confused. Decisions… well, I’ve never been one to make snap decisions anyway. My wife would tell you I can take half an hour choosing something simple, but I think I’ve always been like that.

So no, nothing that feels like a sudden change. I don’t feel like my mind is foggy or that I can’t think straight. Maybe I’m a bit slower, but not in a way that’s worried me.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or hopeless most of the time, or found little pleasure in doing things you used to enjoy?

No, I wouldn’t say that. Not most of the time, anyway. I mean, I have moments where I’m a bit quiet or I sit and think too much, especially when the day’s long and there isn’t much going on, but I don’t feel hopeless as such.

And pleasure… well, I suppose I’m not out doing as much as I used to, but I still get something out of my usual things. I like reading the paper, watching a programme, having things in their place at home. It’s not exciting, maybe, but at my age I don’t expect every day to feel exciting. So no, I haven’t really felt down most days, and I wouldn’t say I’ve lost pleasure in things.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight or appetite recently, such as a significant decrease in appetite or unintentional weight loss?

Well… the weight, yes, the doctor has mentioned that. He says the number on the scale has got too low, or lower than he’d like, anyway. I don’t always see it quite the same way, if I’m honest.

To me, being a bit lighter has made things feel easier in some respects. I can get around the garden without feeling so heavy on my feet, and when I go for my walks I feel like I can keep up with myself better, if that makes sense. I know they look at the number and get concerned, and I’m not saying they’re wrong exactly, but from my point of view it doesn’t feel like some terrible thing. It feels more like I’m just lighter, and that’s made moving about a bit easier.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt little interest or pleasure in doing things most days?

I think I answered that a bit already, didn’t I? No, not most days. I wouldn’t put it that way.

I mean, I’m not running around looking for excitement, and I’m probably quieter than I used to be, but I still do my usual things. I’ll read, putter about a bit, watch something in the evening. Some days are just ordinary days, you know, and I don’t expect to be thrilled by them. But I wouldn’t say I’ve had little interest or no pleasure most days. Nothing like that has really stood out to me.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down, empty, or lost interest in most activities for most of the day, more days than not?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I have quiet patches, certainly, and some days feel a bit flat in the way ordinary days can, especially when there isn’t much happening. But I wouldn’t say I’ve felt down or empty for most of the day, more days than not.

And I haven’t lost interest in most things, not really. I still do my usual bits and pieces, even if they’re not grand activities. So no, I don’t think that fits me.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently without trying to?

Well, I suppose the honest answer is that my doctor says I have, yes. He keeps pointing to the number on the scale and saying it’s got too low, lower than he’s comfortable with. I’m not sure I’d describe it quite the same way, because from my side it doesn’t feel like some dramatic thing I was aiming for.

I mean, I know I’m lighter. I can see that much. But it’s also made certain things feel easier — getting around the garden, bending and moving about, keeping up when I go out for my walks. I don’t feel so weighed down on my feet, if you know what I mean.

So… yes, the number has gone down enough that the doctor is concerned. Whether I’d say it was “without trying,” I don’t know how to put that exactly. I don’t think of it as some big alarming loss the way he does. To me it’s more that being lighter has just felt easier in day-to-day things.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt depressed or lost interest in most activities most of the time?

I’m not sure I can add much more than what I’ve said, really. No, I haven’t felt depressed most of the time these past couple of weeks, at least not in the way I think you mean it. I have my slower moments, and sometimes I sit quietly and don’t feel particularly cheerful, but that doesn’t feel the same as being depressed all day or most days.

And I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in most activities either. I still have my usual routine, the little things I do during the day. They may not sound like much to someone else, but they’re still part of my day, and I do still get something out of them. So if you’re asking whether it’s been most of the time, most days — no, I don’t think that’s true for me.
Have you been through the loss of someone close to you recently, and if so, do you feel that your current mood or behavior is mainly a response to that loss?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve known people who’ve passed away, at my age you can’t really avoid that altogether, but not someone close to me recently in a way that would explain how I’ve been.

So I wouldn’t say my mood or my habits at the moment are because of a bereavement. There isn’t one particular loss I’m reacting to, if that’s what you mean.
Do you find that your mood is particularly low or that you feel less pleasure in things mainly in the morning, more so than at other times of the day?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed a pattern like that, no. Mornings are just… mornings, I suppose. I can be a bit slow getting going sometimes, but I’ve always been that way to some extent, especially now I’m older.

I wouldn’t say I wake up and feel especially low compared with the rest of the day, or that things seem more enjoyable later on in some obvious way. I haven’t really been keeping track of it like that. My mood feels more or less the same across the day, from what I can tell. Nothing stands out to me as being particularly worse in the morning.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty about things more often lately, or feeling like you’re not worth much?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I can feel a bit regretful about ordinary things sometimes — I suppose everyone does, especially when you get older and you’ve had a long life to look back over. You think, “Oh, I could have handled that better,” or “Maybe I should have said something differently.” But I wouldn’t say it’s been happening more often lately in a way that’s weighing on me.

And I don’t really feel worthless, no. I might get frustrated with myself now and then, but that’s different. I don’t sit around thinking I’m no good or that I don’t matter. It’s more just the usual sort of self-criticism, I’d say, not some heavy guilt or feeling like I’m not worth anything.
Over the past two weeks, have you had days where you felt down or experienced little pleasure, and if so, how often did that happen?

I’m not really sure how to answer that exactly. I mean, I’ve had ordinary off days, I suppose — days where I’m a bit flat or not terribly interested in doing much — but I haven’t been counting them, and I wouldn’t want to make it sound more definite than it is.

Over the last couple of weeks, I can’t say there’s been a clear run of days where I felt properly down, or where I couldn’t enjoy anything. It’s more… some days feel a bit dull, but then at my age, some days are just quieter than others. I still have moments where things are pleasant enough. So if you’re asking how often, I’d say not often, or at least not in a way I’ve really noticed as a pattern.
